quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: When it is clear that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if your intentions seem obvious. Signals are always important. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause death.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both brakes smoothly and evenly, without locking up either tire.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has several benefits. Most importantly, choose a position where other drivers can see you and where you have enough space around you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what they need to do.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: A passenger needs to know how to stay safe on a motorcycle. Never assume a passenger already knows what to do. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick one part of the lane and always stay there.
Weave around the lane to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where in the lane they ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Travel on the shoulder to stay away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less traction.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem when the road is wet.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You don't need to look if you check your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume drivers will see your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: You should keep a good distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
So traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or swerve if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on:
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers provide poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle leans to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Approach at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise off the seat so your knees absorb impact. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Be visible to others by using your signals, brake light, and lane position. Maintain space around your motorcycle. Scan the road ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear before riding.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, eye or face protection is not required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is recommended.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Look at the rims and spokes for damage or loose parts. Check the tire condition and tread. Make sure all lights work.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular and white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Motorcycle gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.
